findings.claim: scripts/generate-scorecard-report.py does NOT contain the _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS guard claimed in FIX-ROUND-1.md. R1 COR-MAJ-001 is only half-closed: tools.py (MCP method) received the guard; the markdown generator did not. The generator's main() calls json.loads then render() with no schema_version check anywhere in the file. This means generate-scorecard-report.py still silently processes any schema_version value, directly violating the plan-doc invariant ('Consumers drop indexes with unknown schema_version').
findings.evidence: Grep of scripts/generate-scorecard-report.py for 'schema_version' and '_SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS' returns zero matches. main() lines 202-215: after json.loads at line 202 execution proceeds directly to index.get('aggregated_at') with no schema_version guard. render() lines 82-179: likewise no schema_version check. By contrast, tools.py lines 325-333 correctly contain: _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {'0.1'}; index_schema_version = index.get('schema_version'); if index_schema_version not in _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS: return _error('SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004', ...). FIX-ROUND-1.md §Per-finding disposition COR-MAJ-001 row: 'Added _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {"0.1"} guard to both: generator returns exit 1 + stderr error; MCP returns SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004 error.' The generator half of this claim is not reflected in the code. test_unknown_schema_version_rejected (test_consult_scorecard.py lines 204-219) covers only the MCP method path; no corresponding generator test exists, consistent with the guard being absent.
findings.impact: The plan-doc invariant 2 (schema_version drop on unknown) is still violated for the markdown generator. When the aggregator is upgraded to produce schema_version '0.2', generate-scorecard-report.py silently processes the new layout: render() iterates whatever adopters list it finds and produces a potentially mis-rendered or empty report with a successful exit code 0. The workflow's create-pull-request job then commits a silent wrong report to docs/scorecards/<date>.md with no error annotation. Operators receive no signal of the incompatibility. The MCP method is fixed and will return SCP-MCP-SCORECARD-004; the markdown output is not protected.
findings.mitigation: In scripts/generate-scorecard-report.py main(), after line 202 (json.loads), add: _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {'0.1'}; index_schema_version = index.get('schema_version'); if index_schema_version not in _SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS: print(f'::error file={args.index},title=SCP-E002::unsupported scorecard-index schema_version {index_schema_version!r}; expected one of {sorted(_SUPPORTED_INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSIONS)}', file=sys.stderr); return 1. Add a second parametrized golden-file test case (or a standalone test) in tests/scorecard-report/ that writes an index with schema_version '999.0' and asserts main() returns exit code 1 with no output file written.

findings.claim: The sanitisation ternary ' " " if c in ("\n", "\r") else c' in generate-scorecard-report.py lines 160-163 is dead code for CR/LF. The outer filter 'if c == "\t" or ord(c) >= 0x20' already excludes \n (0x0A) and \r (0x0D) before the ternary is evaluated, so those characters are silently dropped rather than replaced with spaces. The closing comment 'we collapse internal CR/LF to spaces' is inaccurate. The safety goal (no injection) is achieved regardless, so this is not a functional regression — only a misleading comment and unreachable branch.
findings.evidence:
generate-scorecard-report.py lines 159-164: sanitised = ''.join(' ' if c in ('
', '') else c for c in raw_error if c == '	' or ord(c) >= 0x20)[:1500]. ord('

', '') is never True. Comment at line 151: 'we collapse internal CR/LF to spaces'. Actual behaviour: CR/LF characters are dropped entirely (not replaced with a space), which means 'line1
line2' becomes 'line1line2' (words run together) rather than 'line1 line2'. The blockquote injection goal is still met.
findings.impact: No security regression; no markdown injection is possible. The cosmetic impact is that adjacent tokens separated only by newlines merge in the blockquote (e.g. 'error: foo\nreason: bar' renders as 'error: fooreason: bar'). The comment misleads a future maintainer into believing the space-replacement branch is exercised.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) move CR/LF replacement before the filter: sanitised = ''.join(' ' if c in ('\n', '\r') else c for c in raw_error if c in ('\n', '\r') or c == '\t' or ord(c) >= 0x20)[:1500] and update the comment to 'replace CR/LF with space; drop other control chars'; or (b) remove the dead ternary branch and update the comment to 'drop CR/LF and other control chars' — both are safe and honest. No action required before merge if the operator accepts the drop-vs-space distinction.
